newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends higher after short-covering rally.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends higher after short-covering rally.

text.p: A short covering rally triggered by comments from Finance Minister Bill Birch sent the New Zealand dollar 20 basis points higher on Wednesday, the currency retaining its gains by the close.
The Kiwi ended at US$0.6925/32, up substantially from 0.6878/85 at the open and from around 0.6900 just before Birch said in Hong Kong that he thought the Kiwi was not over-valued.
Birch, in an interview with Reuters Financial Television, said some exporters had been under pressure from low commodity prices.
"What I think one should recognise is that, even during this period, say right through calendar '96, our export volumes have steadily moved up.
"We have seen a 10 percent growth of export volumes across the export sector. That is not an indication of an overvalued exchange rate," Birch said.
Birch is in Hong Kong on an investment tour that has also taken him to New York and London.
One senior Auckland dealer said there was very strong buying and that bidding interest had continued going into the close.
"I think it was more that the market was short and I don't think he's said anything different. I just think there were some buyers around and a lot of stops around," he said.
Broadly, he expected the Kiwi to remain in a US$0.6850-0.7000 range, but for US$0.6910-40 to contain the currency overnight.
The Trade-Weighted Index ended at 68.84, up substantially from 68.40 at the open.
